title: Multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices
authors: Sagarika Basak, Xi-Wen Guan, Han Pu
abstract: We investigate the ground-state and dynamical properties of multicomponent interacting anyons confined in a one-dimensional (1D) optical lattice. Adopting the Anyon--Hubbard model, we explore spin and charge correlations as functions of interaction strength and the anyonic statistical parameter. Our results demonstrate that multicomponent effects combined with fractional exchange statistics substantially reshape both charge and spin correlations. For fractional exchange statistics, the canonical symmetric shell structure with prominent singularities in the spinor fermionic momentum distribution undergoes notable structural reconstruction, exhibiting emergent asymmetry, new spectral peaks, and broadened singular features. Unlike the Tonks--Girardeau bosonic gas, pseudobosons, representing a limiting case of anyons, cease to display a dominant zero-momentum peak. Instead, a quasi-fermionic shell structure emerges with finite-momentum peaks, whose locations are modulated by lattice site occupancy and interaction strength. The structure factor of spin correlations uncovers antiferromagnetic ordering in spinor anyon systems, with correlation magnitudes tunable by anyonic exchange statistics. Furthermore, quench dynamics analysis reveals the statistical phase parameter as an effective tuning knob. It enables the switching of dipole oscillations between underdamped and overdamped relaxation regimes and governs overall cloud expansion dynamics. Our findings pave the way for exploring statistics-driven ground-state and dynamical phase transitions in spinor anyon systems.
summary: This paper theoretically explores how multicomponent anyons behave in 1D optical lattices, using the Anyon-Hubbard model. By varying the fractional exchange statistics, the authors show that charge and spin correlations are profoundly altered, leading to novel spectral features and tunable magnetic ordering. The findings establish the statistical phase as a key control knob for both ground-state structure and dynamic behavior.
main_problem: The study investigates the ground-state and dynamical properties of multicomponent interacting anyons confined within a one-dimensional optical lattice.
main_result: The combination of multicomponent effects and fractional exchange statistics significantly reshapes charge and spin correlations, leading to emergent asymmetry and tunable magnetic ordering.
method: The analysis uses theoretical mapping to a generalized Anyon-Hubbard model, employing techniques like Jordan-Wigner transformations and DMRG simulations.
model_or_system: The system models multicomponent anyons interacting in a 1D optical lattice, governed by an Anyon-Hubbard Hamiltonian. The statistics are controlled by a fractional statistical phase parameter, $	heta$.
key_observables: Charge and spin correlations, momentum distribution ($\hat{n}_k$), spin structure factor ($S(k)$), and dipole oscillation dynamics.
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($U$), anyonic statistical parameter ($	heta$), and lattice site occupancy.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to one-dimensional systems, and the mapping assumes anticommutation on the same site.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the fermionic representation of the anyon system and compare intrinsic anyonic momentum distributions ($\hat{n}_k$) with observable physical-fermion distributions ($\hat{n}_O^k$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the model and mapping it to a fermionic description, analyzing ground-state correlations (charge/spin) across different statistical regimes, and finally examining quench dynamics to show the tunability of the system's response.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physics of strongly correlated quantum gases using anyonic statistics, which is a major frontier in ultracold atom research, especially concerning spin and charge correlations.
